## Summary

**Bug (stale-audit correctness gap).** `_compute_content_fingerprint` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, ~line 696) fingerprints only: git HEAD sha + work-item description hash + Key Files list. However, the audit's own file-scope manifest reads `git status --porcelain` (untracked/modified files) and the deep-analysis model reads the **working tree**, not just HEAD. So uncommitted code changes between audits do **not** invalidate freshness — the freshness gate can serve a stale audit for code that has since changed.

The docs claim "a change in ANY fingerprint component invalidates freshness", but working-tree state is not a component.

## Expected behaviour

Include the working-tree state in the fingerprint payload: a hash of `git status --porcelain` + `git diff --name-only HEAD` output (sorted, deterministic). A change in any uncommitted file, untracked file, or commit invalidates freshness; an untouched repo keeps the same fingerprint.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Modifying an uncommitted tracked file invalidates the fingerprint (stale audit → re-run).
2. Adding an untracked file invalidates the fingerprint.
3. Committing a change also invalidates (via the existing HEAD sha component).
4. An untouched working tree + unchanged description + unchanged Key Files keeps the same fingerprint (freshness preserved).
5. Unit tests cover all four cases; `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/` passes green.
data.title: Include working-tree state in the audit content fingerprint (stale-audit gap)

## Summary

`skill/audit/SKILL.md` lines 22–24 document a "Pre-flight affirmation": "Verify absence before proceeding to the audit flow. Confirm that the work item is ready for audit and that no active conflicting processes exist." **No code implements this.**

The concurrency semaphore (`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`) caps concurrent pi subprocesses host-wide, but does not prevent two audits of the **same** work item racing: both set `in_progress`, both run the pipeline, and the last writer wins on persist + status transition.

## Expected behaviour

Decide and implement one of:
- **Implement:** a cheap guard in `cmd_issue` — if the item's status is already `in_progress` at entry (i.e. someone/something else is mid-audit) and `--force` is not given, warn and abort (or wait) instead of racing.
- **Remove:** rewrite the SKILL.md section to describe the actual behavior (status lifecycle + concurrency cap only).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Docs and code no longer diverge: either the guard is implemented and tested, or the SKILL.md section is corrected.
2. If implemented: an `in_progress` item without `--force` does not start a competing audit; `--force` bypasses the guard; the status lifecycle otherwise unchanged.
3. `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/` green.
data.title: Implement or remove the unimplemented Pre-flight affirmation

## Summary

`_check_audit_freshness` and `_get_child_audit_verdict` in `audit_runner.py` duplicate ~25 lines each of identical ISO-8601 timestamp handling: normalize `Z` suffix → `datetime.fromisoformat` → make tz-aware (UTC fallback) → compare against `updatedAt + AUDIT_FRESHNESS_BUFFER_SECONDS`. Drift between the two has already been a source of bugs (e.g. the persistence-write tolerance, SA-0MSI3XH34001LLU4).

## Expected behaviour

Extract a shared helper (e.g. `_parse_iso_utc(value) -> datetime | None` and/or `_audit_is_fresh(audited_at, updated_at) -> bool`) used by both functions, preserving the `AUDIT_PERSIST_WRITE_TOLERANCE_SECONDS` semantics in `_get_child_audit_verdict`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Single timestamp-parse/compare implementation; both callers use it.
2. Freshness tests (content gate, time gate, persistence-tolerance) pass unchanged.
3. `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/` green.
data.title: Share ISO-8601 freshness timestamp parsing between freshness helpers

## Summary

`cmd_issue` performs several redundant `wl show` fetches of the same work item:
1. `wl show` (capture original status/stage)
2. `wl show --children` (main pipeline)
3. `_check_audit_freshness` may issue another `wl show` (time-gate path)
4. Per child: `_get_child_audit_verdict` issues `wl show` for freshness; the auto-trigger loop may call `_check_audit_freshness` again for the same child

Each is a subprocess spawn plus (without the worklog-dir cache, see the cache work item) a sibling-dir scan.

## Expected behaviour

Pass already-fetched work-item data through callers where the data is available (e.g. `_check_audit_freshness` accepts a `work_item` argument like `_compute_content_fingerprint` already does). Do not change wl command semantics or freshness behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

1. No duplicate `wl show` of the same item where the data is already in hand; measured per-run `wl` subprocess count for a single-child audit drops (test instrumented via the injectable runner).
2. Freshness and status-capture behavior unchanged.
3. `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/` green.
data.title: Reduce redundant wl show fetches during item audits

## Summary

`cmd_issue` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` is ~1,200 lines. It orchestrates: freshness gate, code-quality check, Phase 1 parent AC screening, Phase 1 child screening (parallel), the parent-first vs `--audit-children` flows, the auto-trigger cascade, Phase 2 (deep/batch), persistence + readback, and the verdict-driven status lifecycle. The `if audit_children:` / `else:` parent-first split is the densest nesting and the most error-prone to modify.

## Expected behaviour

Decompose into ~5–6 named phases (e.g. fetch+gate, code quality, phase1, phase2, persist, lifecycle) as module-level functions operating on a small context dataclass. Strictly behavior-preserving — this is a refactor, not a feature change. The 344-test suite is the safety net.

## Acceptance criteria

1. No behavior change: full audit test suite passes without test modifications (except where tests reference internal structure).
2. `cmd_issue` is meaningfully smaller; each phase is independently testable.
3. `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/` green.
data.title: Decompose cmd_issue (~1200 lines) into named phases

# Guard contract tests and guard-fires proof

## Goal

Author the failing-first tests that pin the sandbox invariant, the snapshot/compare contract,
and both guard entry points — including the executable proof that the guard fires on a
live-repo mutation (F1 AC4 fallback; parent AC2 + AC3 verification).

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (sandbox)** Unit tests for `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` prove: a target path inside any
  git work tree is rejected; a `tmp_path` directory is accepted; a repo created by the factory
  resolves `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` under `tmp_path`; a migrated fixture repo has no
  remote pointing at the repository's real `origin`. *Verification:* `pytest skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`.
- **AC2 (snapshot contract)** Unit tests prove the snapshot/compare helper reports: an added ref,
  a deleted ref, a moved ref (e.g. `refs/heads/dev` advanced), a changed local `.git/config` key,
  a deleted tracked file, and a newly added untracked non-ignored top-level entry — and reports
  nothing for an unchanged repo. *Verification:* same test module.
- **AC3 (guard-fires proof — conftest entry point)** A subprocess test runs pytest **as the
  session root** inside a `tmp_path` git repo whose single test mutates that repo (creates a
  branch); the guard aborts the session non-zero and names the offending test. The nested repo
  arms the guard via its own conftest included from the shared plugin module. *Verification:*
  `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py`.
- **AC4 (guard-fires proof — run_tests entry point)** A subprocess test runs
  `run_tests.py` against a `tmp_path` git repo whose configured test command mutates a ref; the
  run exits non-zero. *Verification:* same test module.
- **AC5 (no false positives)** A test that creates branches/worktrees in an unrelated `tmp_path`
  repo does NOT trip the guard, and a no-op run reports clean. Covers the parent constraint that
  legitimate `tmp_path` repositories and `.worklog/worktrees/wl-*` agent worktrees must not
  false-positive.
- **AC6 (red is behavioural) — ADJUSTED (producer variance, 2026-09-27):** the historical
  "tests fail behaviourally before F3-F5 land" property is accepted as satisfied by the recorded
  2026-09-25 red run and by the met AC7 (behavioural assertions only, no collection errors). The
  retained, verifiable requirement is that the sandbox/guard tests assert observable behaviour and
  never fail with a bare collection error caused by a missing module.
- **AC7** No source-text/grep assertions: the tests assert observable behaviour only (per
  `skill/shared/test-writing-guidelines.md` anti-pattern 1).

- **Covers parent **AC1 — Hermetic git usage:** every test helper that runs real `git` commands
- **Covers parent **AC3 — Regression guard:** `run_tests.py --scope full` snapshots the main


## Key Files

- `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py` (new) — sandbox + snapshot contract tests.
- `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py` (new) — both guard entry points, guard-fires proof, no-false-positive test.

## Notes

- "Red before F3-F5, green after" is intentionally NOT an AC here (unverifiable at close);
  F3/F4/F5 each own "its slice is green" and F7 owns whole-suite green.
- Mutating the live checkout to obtain the proof is forbidden; the guard is tested in a
  subprocess whose session root is a `tmp_path` repo.
data.title: Guard contract tests and guard-fires proof

2. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes.

## Suggested Triage Steps

2. If reproducible, assign to `Build` and route for triage.

Build (confidence: 0.0, reason: no owner inference available)

## Links

- Runbook: skill/triage/resources/runbook-test-failure.md
- CI artifacts: (not available)

## Root-Cause Analysis (plan — 2026-09-26)

The target test passes on the latest `dev` (`1590f470`):

```
python3 -m pytest -q "skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py::TestLifecycleVerification::test_swallowed_no_update_fails_nonzero"
# 1 passed
```

At the recorded failing commit `10995367` the launch-context guard
(`audit_runner._verify_launch_context`) rejected the mocked `TEST-1` item:

```
Audit launch-context error: work item TEST-1 is owned by project /tmp/wlfields-test
(resolved from the worklog prefix scan), but this run was launched from project ...
```

`_verify_launch_context` resolves the owning project via
`skill.shared.status_lifecycle._find_worklog_dir_by_prefix`, whose scan root is
`SIBLING_SCAN_ROOT = REPO_ROOT.parent`. A stale sibling `TEST`-prefixed worklog
(`/tmp/wlfields-test/.worklog`) therefore mis-resolved `TEST-1` in checkouts
whose parent directory contains it. Commit `10995367` itself fixed the
underlying `_resolve_owning_checkout_root` resolution (removal of the accidental
nested `skill/skill` symlink plus the defensive walk) — the target test passes on
`dev` after that fix, and the full audit suite reports no failure for this test.

**Residual risk / verification note:** `test_audit_runner_launch_context.py` can
leave `/tmp/wlfields-test` behind, which makes these mocked `TEST-1` tests
environment-dependent (they fail when the checkout's parent contains that
sibling). AC1 (test passes on latest `dev`) is already satisfied; implementation
should confirm this and, if the stale-sibling isolation issue reproduces, tighten
the prefix scan fallback rather than changing the lifecycle logic.

## Key Files
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_verify_launch_context`, `cmd_issue` terminal transition
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_lifecycle.py` — target test
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `_find_worklog_dir_by_prefix`, `_resolve_owning_checkout_root`
- `skill/shared/tests/test_resolve_repo_root.py` — REPO_ROOT resolution regression coverage

## Summary

Add a fail-fast refusal to the pre-push/release gate path (approved Q1 option d): scrubbing happens everywhere, but only the release gate refuses to proceed when repository-override variables are present in its environment.

**Target outcome:** the ship/release test gate aborts loudly with an actionable message when `GIT_DIR` (or another override var) is present, instead of silently proceeding into a run where a bug in the scrub would be catastrophic.

**Definition of done:** `run_tests.py` supports a strict mode that exits non-zero with a clear message when override vars are present; the release gate invokes it in strict mode; a documented opt-out exists for the rare legitimate case.

**Constraints:** ad-hoc developer/agent `run_tests.py` and `audit_runner.py` invocations must NOT be refused (they scrub + warn per F3); the existing detect-only live-repo guard (F4/F5, SA-0MUG30J5F001L57H) remains as the inner net.

**Risky assumptions:** that the release gate is the correct single strict point. If the ship skill executes the suite through a different entry point, that entry point must be updated too.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A strict flag (e.g. `--strict-git-env`) makes `run_tests.py` exit non-zero with a message naming the offending variables, before any suite command runs.
- [ ] The pre-push/release gate invokes the suite in strict mode (documented in the ship skill).
- [ ] Without the strict flag, `run_tests.py` does not refuse; it scrubs and warns (F3 behaviour).
- [ ] An explicit, documented opt-out env var allows an operator to bypass strict mode with a loud warning.
- [ ] Tests cover: strict mode with a var present (refuse), strict mode clean (proceed), non-strict with a var present (proceed + warn).

**Key Files:**
- skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py
- skill/ship/scripts/release/merge-dev-to-main.sh
- skill/ship/SKILL.md
- tests/test_run_tests_cache.py

**Dependencies:** F2 (helper), F3 (scrub behaviour).
**Deliverables:** strict pre-flight guard + release-gate wiring + tests + docs.
data.title: Release-gate fail-fast on repository-override vars

## Summary

Wire the shared scrub into every production path that spawns a test subprocess so a leaked `GIT_DIR` is neutralised at the source, plus a diagnostic log naming any stripped variables.

**Target outcome:** `test_cache._default_runner`, `run_tests._run_cmd`/`_cached_runner`, and the audit suite-invocation and pi-launch paths all pass a scrubbed environment to `subprocess.run`/`Popen`.

**Definition of done:** every test-spawning subprocess in the test and audit skills receives a scrubbed env; a startup diagnostic records which override vars were stripped (without leaking values); existing PATH/`~/.local/bin` injection behaviour is preserved.

**Constraints:** no behaviour change beyond env scrubbing; cache keys and command strings unchanged; must not break the recursion marker handshake (`LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE`).

**Risky assumptions:** that the audit pi-launch `Popen` path is on the test-execution surface; verified by inspection, but a test must assert the scrubbed env is passed.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `test_cache._default_runner` obtains its env via the F2 helper instead of a bare `os.environ.copy()`.
- [ ] `run_tests._run_cmd` (and `_cached_runner`, which delegates to it) passes an explicit scrubbed `env=` (currently inherits the parent env).
- [ ] `audit_runner` passes a scrubbed env to both the suite invocation and the pi-launch `Popen` path.
- [ ] A diagnostic line naming the stripped override variables is emitted once at runner startup when any were present, and is silent otherwise.
- [ ] Existing runner env behaviour (`~/.local/bin` on `PATH`, unrelated vars preserved) is unchanged, covered by tests.
- [ ] The startup diagnostic records only the stripped variable names, never their values.
- [ ] Cache keys, command strings, and the `LIVE_REPO_GUARD_ACTIVE` recursion-marker handshake are unchanged by the scrub (asserted by test).
- [ ] F1 regression tests pass with these changes applied.

- [ ] Parent AC traceability: `test_cache._default_runner` (and `run_tests.py`/`audit_runner.py`) remove `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_WORK_TREE`, `GIT_CONFIG*`, `GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY`, `GIT_ALTERNATE_OBJECT_DIRECTORIES` before spawning tests.
**Key Files:**
- skill/test_cache.py
- skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py
- skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py

**Dependencies:** F1, F2.
**Deliverables:** production env scrub + diagnostic logging + tests.
